title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a compliance failure at the physical layer of a deployment, not a failure of a model or a dataset. The equipment was installed and operated before the authorisation that its use required existed, and the site was already partly in use when state inspectors found it. The gap is between building and being allowed to run, and it was closed only after the fact.

Catching it would have required a permit check at two points that already existed on paper: before installation and before operation. The inspection that produced the finding happened in late July, which means the state's verification step was real but sequenced after the generators were already in place. A pre-installation review, or an inspection triggered when the first units went in, would have surfaced the same absence earlier and at lower cost.

What is not established is intent. The fine is an administrative penalty under the Air Pollution Control Act, not a court finding, and the homeowners' federal lawsuit over noise is an allegation that has not been adjudicated. The health department's violation orders are separate regulatory actions, and none of these establish that the operator knew the permits were missing.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 natural gas generators at its Vineland data center site in late July. None of the 2,000 kilowatt generators had the required permits to be installed or operated. Officials said the penalty was the largest ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey for violating the Air Pollution Control Act.

The Vineland campus is scheduled to be finished at the end of the year. It will be 2.6 million square feet and require 350 megawatts of power, enough for a medium size city. Some of the complex is already in use. Homeowners have filed a federal lawsuit over noise, and the Cumberland County Health Department has issued violation orders for excessive noise.
